input: Prepare me for a meeting with Attio (attio.com)

challenges.evidence: July 2026 G2 review 'A CRM for Small Businesses not Scaling': 'Attio is missing several standard features, such as field permissions, validation rules, and currencies with conversions'; Nov 2025 Capterra: 'missing attribute options such as formula fields. missing reporting functionality.' Techreviewer (Sept 2026) rated functionality and reliability 'Mixed'.
challenges.challenge: Product gaps for scaling/mid-market users — missing field permissions, validation rules, currency conversion, formula fields and deeper reporting, drawing 'not yet a CRM' criticism.

challenges.evidence: May 2026 G2 review: 'The outreach feature is terrible. Being limited to 12 emails per hour just isn't usable at all'; users 'consistently cite missing native integrations'; Salesforce AppExchange has 9,000+ partner apps vs Attio's ~100 native integrations.
challenges.challenge: Automation/outreach limits and integration gaps vs HubSpot and Salesforce — tight email-sequence caps, no on-demand enrichment, no native LinkedIn Sales Navigator, and a far smaller ecosystem (~100 native integrations vs HubSpot's 1,500+ apps).

challenges.evidence: 'Attio's flexibility creates a cost. The same customization users praise makes automation setup harder'; RFP.wiki (July 2026) warns 'credit consumption on AI-heavy workflows can surprise buyers'; live pricing is $35/$79 vs older $29/$69 shown on G2/Capterra.
challenges.challenge: Setup burden and pricing friction as it moves upmarket — flexible data model demands significant setup/ongoing maintenance, AI-heavy workflows consume credits unpredictably, and recent price rises ($35 Plus / $79 Pro) outdate third-party listings.

challenges.evidence: Competitor review site (Oct 12, 2026) markets a 'companion layer' alternative: 'Teams already on Salesforce or HubSpot can get similar flexibility by layering a companion solution on top of their existing CRM instead of switching.' Attio itself acknowledges rivals 'racing to add AI features'.
challenges.challenge: Intensifying AI-CRM competition — a wave of AI-first challengers (e.g. Coffee positioning itself as a no-migration companion layer to Salesforce/HubSpot) and incumbents racing to bolt AI onto legacy CRMs.

key_people.name: Nicolas Sharp
key_people.title: Co-founder & CEO
key_people.recent: Authored the Oct 2026 'architecture for agentic revenue' launch and the $52M Series B announcement; hosts 4x-ARR-growth narrative with 5,000+ paying customers.

key_people.name: Alexander Christie
key_people.title: Co-founder & CTO
key_people.recent: Technology co-founder behind the hybrid 'people + agents' architecture (SQL Engine, Data Connectors, Agent Scale) published Oct 2026.

key_people.name: Michael McBride
key_people.title: General Partner at GV; Attio board member (former CRO of GitLab)
key_people.recent: Led Attio's $52M Series B (Aug 2025), joined the board, and wrote the GV thesis 'From Legacy to AI-Native' about reinventing CRM for the AI era.

key_people.name: Drew Peterson
key_people.title: Vice President of Sales & Success
key_people.recent: Leads the sales and success org per the public org chart; likely owner of any conversation about GTM tooling and CRM consolidation.

key_people.name: Alex Vale
key_people.title: VP of Marketing
key_people.recent: Owns marketing during the agentic-revenue repositioning (homepage now headlines 'Welcome to agentic revenue').

priorities.evidence: CEO Nicolas Sharp blog, Oct 2026: 'Attio is introducing a new shape of software. It is the first hybrid architecture engineered for people and agents in equal measure. We're launching four new capabilities: SQL Engine, Data Connectors, Agent Scale, and Activities, in beta.'
priorities.priority: Ship the 'architecture for agentic revenue' — four new capabilities (SQL Engine, Data Connectors, Agent Scale, Activities in beta) extending its hybrid platform for people and agents.

priorities.evidence: 'Workflows is Attio's engine to orchestrate AI agents alongside your team... Workflows is live today' (Jun 2026); Sept 23, 2026 changelog adds 'Workflow history and agent log' and 'New blocks for workflows'.
priorities.priority: Scale Workflows as the engine for orchestrating AI revenue agents on every account (launched live June 2026; ongoing updates Sept–Oct 2026: workflow history/agent log, new blocks).

priorities.evidence: Feb 2026 launch post: 'We are launching Ask Attio, a new way to work with your entire CRM... Universal Context, a unified intelligence layer we've built that semantically indexes everything in your CRM as one interconnected whole.'
priorities.priority: Universal Context / Ask Attio — a unified intelligence layer that semantically indexes everything in the CRM so users can query it conversationally.

priorities.evidence: 'With its Series B, Attio will scale engineering, fast-track product development'; founder blog: '5,000 paying customers now run their go-to-market on Attio... on track to 4x ARR growth this year.'
priorities.priority: Deploy the $52M Series B (led by GV) to scale engineering, fast-track product development, and push the 4x-ARR-growth motion with 5,000+ paying customers.

priorities.evidence: 'With our App SDK, now in beta, builders are deploying custom apps directly inside Attio'; Oct 29, 2026 changelog: 'Developer changelog is live'.
priorities.priority: Grow the developer/ecosystem surface — App SDK in beta, MCP support, partner app blocks (Linear, Fin), plus a developer changelog and live 'How Attio uses Attio' community workshops.

what_they_do.value: Attio is a relational, AI-native CRM for go-to-market teams — a platform that builds pipeline, advances deals and grows accounts around the clock, now positioned as 'the platform for agentic revenue'.

recent_changes.summary: Large coordinated release: Activities ('Capture anything that moves a deal'), redesigned record pages, a new inbox, and Workflows updates — plus the developer changelog going live.
recent_changes.headline: Attio changelog, October 29, 2026: five feature drops incl. Activities and redesigned record pages

recent_changes.summary: CEO Nicolas Sharp announced the 'architecture for agentic revenue': SQL Engine, Data Connectors, Agent Scale, and Activities (beta) — the company's biggest positioning shift this year.
recent_changes.headline: Introducing the architecture for Agentic Revenue (Attio blog, Oct 2026)

recent_changes.summary: Workflow history and agent log shipped — 'full visibility into every run, down to the agent' — alongside new conversation-to-action blocks and app updates.
recent_changes.headline: Workflow history and agent log

recent_changes.summary: Raised $52M Series B led by GV (with Redpoint, Balderton, Point Nine, 01A), taking total funding to $116M; GV's Michael McBride joined the board. Within the last ~14 months this is the anchor corporate event behind the current roadmap.
recent_changes.headline: Attio Raises $52M Series B to Scale the First AI-Native CRM for Go-to-Market Builders

talking_points: Activities shipped Oct 29, 2026 as the newest beta layer of the agentic-revenue architecture — ask how Attio plans to source support-ticket, product-event and social-DM data (build vs partner), and where a data/intelligence vendor could close the enrichment gaps users already complain about (no on-demand enrichment, no direct dials, no intent signals).

Attio says rivals are 'racing to add AI features' while it rebuilds the foundation — probe what will make teams already standardized on Salesforce/HubSpot switch, given reviews flagging missing field permissions, validation rules and multi-currency as blockers for mid-market deals.

With Workflows billing '9 in 10 block runs free' and AI charged by model usage, ask how customers are reacting to usage-based AI costs — RFP.wiki flagged credit-consumption surprises as a buyer concern, and pricing transparency is a live objection Attio must manage.

Attio is on track to 4x ARR growth with 5,000+ paying customers, mostly startups like Lovable, Granola and Modal — ask how the go-to-market motion evolves for mid-market/enterprise buyers, and which partnerships (integrations, data, services) leadership sees filling its ~100-integration ecosystem gap.
